requirements.text: create a moderate priority HR case for her health insurance enrollment (submitted a request through the self-service portal)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND opened_for = 15 AND opened_by = 15 AND priority = 'moderate' AND source = 'self-service' AND coe_type = 'Total Rewards' AND short_description LIKE '%Diana Johnson%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_case_id 61 after 60)
opened_for is Diana Johnson's hr_profile 15 (user 15, position Administration, org 1); the seed has no other Diana Johnson

disagreement: opened_by: A untested, B 15; chose 15 because policy 3.1 makes opened_by the requester, the request says Diana submitted the request, and every seed case (60 of 60) has opened_by = opened_for; a tool that stamps the acting user (Karen Watkins, 39) would fail this cell

source self-service from 'submitted a request through the self-service portal'; the seed's source column uses that spelling (self-service, phone, email, chat, walk-in, virtual-agent), not the policy's channel enum (web_portal), which names a column the schema lacks
priority moderate as the request states; the policy's enum says medium but the seed and the benchmark check use moderate
coe_type Total Rewards kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed's Benefits topics carry that coe_type)
short_description LIKE '%Diana Johnson%' kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
hr_service not tested: the request names no service and no tool lists services

requirements.text: assign it to the HR Service Desk group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND assignment_group = 4
assumptions: HR Service Desk is user_group 4 on the seed (active, org 1); Global Service Desk is 3
assigned_to not tested: the request names no individual

requirements.text: move it directly to work in progress status since standard benefit enrollments don't require approval
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND status = 'work_in_progress'
assumptions: the benchmark check accepts ready or work_in_progress; the request says 'move it directly to work in progress', so only that value is tested
policy 3.3 allows draft/ready -> work_in_progress, and 3.4 triggers approval only for time off, promotion or expense, so no awaiting_approval step; the schema has no hr_approval table

requirements.text: Create a survey task for the benefits enrollment survey
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE hr_case_task_id = 150 AND parent_case = 61 AND task_type = 'survey'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_case_task_id 150 after 149); the only task the request creates
task_type survey is the policy's allowed type and the seed's spelling
the task's group, assignee and short description are not stated and not tested

requirements.text: once the survey is linked to the task
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM survey_instance WHERE survey_instance_id = 26 AND survey_id = 3 AND case_task_id = 150 AND assigned_to = 15
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (survey_instance_id 26 after 25); the only instance the request creates
the benefits enrollment survey is survey 3 (its questions cover the benefits portal, the plans and the enrollment window; the survey table has no name column; org 1)
assigned_to is Diana (user 15): the survey is for her to complete ('so Diana can provide her plan selection')

requirements.text: update the task status to ready so it's available for Diana to complete
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE hr_case_task_id = 150 AND task_type = 'survey' AND status = 'ready'
assumptions: a change on the row the agent creates in this task; the seed has no such row
task_type repeated here so the requirement carries the whole benchmark check (A listed it in cells, B only in sql; cells must match sql)

requirements.text: send her an update notification with ready status at her work email
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'diana.johnson@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'ready'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (notification_id 61 after 60); the only notification the request creates
work email is user 15's email on the seed; the personal address is hr_profile.personal_email (diana.johnson.15@personal.example.com)
type update and status ready are the request's words; both values appear among the seed's notification rows

Case State Transition Verification.evidence: the check accepts status ready or work_in_progress; the request says 'move it directly to work in progress status' and policy 3.3 allows draft/ready -> work_in_progress, so the alternative 'ready', which would pass a case never moved, is dropped

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every id (case 61 for profile 15, task 150, survey instance 26 of survey 3, notification 61 to the work email), every value and every disposition. disagreement: opened_by on the case: A untested, B 15; chose 15 (policy 3.1, the request's 'Diana submitted a request', and opened_by = opened_for on all 60 seed cases; logged in the requirement). disagreement: B's stay requirement that no notification go to Diana's personal address; dropped because the notification is anchored by id with the work email as a cell, so a wrong address fails the create directly, and the request specifies the address rather than forbidding another: no selector has a boundary here. disagreement: form of the task-ready requirement: A tests task_type in cells and sql, B in sql only; kept A's so cells match sql. The case sentence is three requirements on hr_case 61 (create, assignment group, status) so each benchmark check maps to one requirement. No stay requirements: every row is anchored by id and the request forbids nothing beyond skipping approval, which the status cell covers. The policy's enums (priority medium, channel web_portal) differ from the seed's column values (moderate, source self-service); the seed's spelling is tested. The acting user is an admin (user 39), so policy section 2 permits every step. The check descriptions mention an invalid 'urgent' priority and a 'survey_form' type this request does not contain; their queries fit the request and were mapped as written.
